Arizona State Sun Devils.status: Transfer — from Kentucky, replacing Sam Leavitt, who left for Lane Kiffin at LSU.
Arizona State Sun Devils.career_experience: Kentucky's starter; the guide describes him as up and down in that role.
Arizona State Sun Devils.previous_starts: Not addressed in guide as a start count.
Arizona State Sun Devils.passing: 2,160 yards with 15 touchdowns and 12 interceptions at Kentucky.
Arizona State Sun Devils.rushing: Not addressed in guide as production; the guide credits above-average athleticism.
Arizona State Sun Devils.efficiency: Not addressed in guide as a completion rate.
Arizona State Sun Devils.competition: None described — Boley is presented as the starter.
Arizona State Sun Devils.author_confidence: Positive and explicitly contextual. The guide is careful to note he had an unreliable supporting cast and no one of Dillingham's reputation at Kentucky, and expects the group to exceed expectations.
Arizona State Sun Devils.positive_case: 6-foot-5 with a big arm and above-average athleticism; Dillingham once tried to recruit him to Oregon, which the guide reads as genuine belief. It cites his tools, an improved offensive line and receiver weapons.
Arizona State Sun Devils.concerns: Up-and-down Kentucky production including 12 interceptions, and the guide's note that he may need time to settle.
Arizona State Sun Devils.scheme_fit: Complicated by a play-calling question the guide raises separately: Dillingham mostly called plays in 2024 and Arizona State averaged 6.1 yards per play; with Marcus Arroyo calling them last year that fell to 5.6.
Arizona State Sun Devils.supporting_cast: Improving — an improved offensive line and receiver weapons including Boston College transfer Reed Harris.
Arizona State Sun Devils.portal_context: Boley in from Kentucky, Reed Harris in from Boston College; Sam Leavitt out to LSU. The guide draws the pattern that last year's team lost Cam Skattebo and this year's loses Leavitt — two core pieces of the 2024 side.
Arizona State Sun Devils.betting_implications: Recommendation is Over 6.5 wins. The guide judges Arizona State unlikely to return to the playoff soon but not going anywhere either, says Dillingham keeps reloading well, and states a 6.5 total simply does not feel right. It names the winnable games explicitly and says the Sun Devils may be live for alternate Overs too.
Arizona State Sun Devils.outlook_dependency: Moderate to high. The Over rests on reloading well after Leavitt's departure, with Boley the named replacement, but the guide's argument is roster-wide rather than quarterback-specific.
Arizona State Sun Devils.conflicts: The team spread (p. 118) prints 17 returning starters while the Stability Score table (p. 42) prints 12 for the same team. Both are reproduced as printed in the Team Database and neither is corrected here.

Arizona Wildcats.career_experience: Established starter; the guide contrasts a poor 2024 with a major bounceback in 2025.
Arizona Wildcats.previous_starts: Not addressed in guide as a start count.
Arizona Wildcats.passing: 3,228 yards with 29 touchdowns and six interceptions; PFF's 17th-ranked passer.
Arizona Wildcats.efficiency: PFF's 17th-ranked passer — described as a major bounceback from a poor 2024.
Arizona Wildcats.competition: None described — Fifita is the settled starter and is called a star.
Arizona Wildcats.author_confidence: Positive but deliberately withheld. The guide calls him one of the top returning starters, then explicitly declines the easy conclusion and lists three reasons for doubt.
Arizona Wildcats.positive_case: 3,228 yards with a 29-to-6 touchdown-to-interception ratio, solid weapons, a decent run game and an established rapport with returning coordinator Seth Doege.
Arizona Wildcats.concerns: Three, stated as a list: the 2024 season is hard to ignore entirely, Arizona must replace three offensive line starters, and Fifita occasionally has injury trouble. Its closing caution is that replicating or building on 2025 is the hope — but that is also what Tucson hoped for in 2024.
Arizona Wildcats.scheme_fit: Continuity — an established rapport with returning coordinator Seth Doege.
Arizona Wildcats.supporting_cast: Solid weapons and a decent run game, offset by three offensive line starters to replace.
Arizona Wildcats.portal_context: The guide credits Brennan's portal work as strong at programme level; it does not describe portal additions at quarterback.
Arizona Wildcats.betting_implications: Recommendation is Under 7.5 wins. Arizona will be an underdog against BYU and Texas Tech and plays six further games the guide treats as coin flips, so eight wins feels unrealistic even if the team is as good as last year's. A regression argument is added explicitly — a +18 turnover margin last year, some of which the guide expects to come back.
Arizona Wildcats.outlook_dependency: High. Expectations are stated as somewhat high specifically because Fifita is back, and the guide's turnover-regression argument bears directly on the position.
Arizona Wildcats.conflicts: The team page (p. 116) prints 12 returning starters while the Stability Score table (p. 42) prints 14 for the same team. Both are reproduced as printed in the Team Database and neither is corrected here.

BYU Cougars.status: Returning starter — seized the job as a freshman.
BYU Cougars.career_experience: Was not meant to start as a freshman but seized the job.
BYU Cougars.previous_starts: Not addressed in guide as a start count.
BYU Cougars.passing: 3,033 yards with 15 touchdowns and seven interceptions.
BYU Cougars.efficiency: An overall PFF grade of 78.9, top 50 — but the guide stresses his 77.0 rushing grade is what raised the profile.
BYU Cougars.competition: None described — Bachmeier is the settled starter.
BYU Cougars.author_confidence: Positive with a precisely stated development target. The guide's diagnosis is that he was far more comfortable running than passing, and that if the passing grade surpasses the rushing grade, BYU has something special.
BYU Cougars.positive_case: Genuine dual-threat production as a freshman on a 12-win team returning nearly every impactful player.
BYU Cougars.concerns: Passing development is the named gap, and the guide draws out a compounding problem: he must develop as a passer while working without receivers he is comfortable with.
BYU Cougars.supporting_cast: Weakened at receiver. Parker Kingston had 97 catches for 928 yards and five touchdowns and BYU hoped to keep the shifty slot man, but he was expelled from school over off-field conduct, leaving heavy reliance on an unproven group. Oregon transfer Kyle Kasper is flagged as one to watch — a 6-foot-6 contested-catch target who moves well for his size.
BYU Cougars.portal_context: Kyle Kasper arrives at receiver from Oregon.
BYU Cougars.betting_implications: Recommendation is Over 8.5 wins. The guide allows that things can be nitpicked but says the squad clearly has the goods, and makes a market observation: hosting Notre Dame may be the only game all season in which the Cougars receive points, with a possible exception at Utah on 7 November.
BYU Cougars.outlook_dependency: High. The guide's stated upside — BYU having something special — is conditional on Bachmeier's passing grade surpassing his rushing grade.

Baylor Bears.career_experience: The top-ranked quarterback in the 2024 class and once seen as Florida's saviour, with strong early film before the season turned.
Baylor Bears.previous_starts: Not addressed in guide as a start count.
Baylor Bears.passing: Not addressed in guide as a yardage line; the guide reports 14 interceptions and 19 sacks last year.
Baylor Bears.efficiency: Not addressed in guide; the guide credits deep-ball touch.
Baylor Bears.turnovers: 14 interceptions last year, which the guide characterizes as too many mistakes at the most important position.
Baylor Bears.competition: None described — Lagway is presented as the starter.
Baylor Bears.author_confidence: Optimistic and explicitly conditional. The guide credits accumulated injuries as a factor, agrees a change of scenery was needed, and sees a major turnaround available conditional on the line keeping him upright.
Baylor Bears.positive_case: The top-ranked quarterback in his class, now with an elite play-caller in Jake Spavital, inheriting an offense that scored 31.1 points per game. The guide notes Sawyer Robertson put up big numbers in this system and rates Lagway arguably more talented, with deep-ball touch likely to produce big plays in a scheme known for receivers running free.
Baylor Bears.concerns: 14 interceptions and 19 sacks last year — too many mistakes at the most important position — with the turnaround conditional on protection.
Baylor Bears.scheme_fit: Explicitly favourable — a more quarterback-friendly offense under an elite play-caller.
Baylor Bears.supporting_cast: A revamped offensive line must protect him: Kaden Sieracki returns at right tackle with four new faces elsewhere, three of them previous starters. The guide expects Baylor to be bigger and deeper up front with real potential for improvement.
Baylor Bears.portal_context: Lagway is the high-profile portal addition; the line was substantially rebuilt.
Baylor Bears.betting_implications: Recommendation is Over 5.5 wins. The guide states the stakes bluntly: with a tough schedule and a 5.5 total, failure to cash the Over likely means Aranda is looking for a defensive coordinator job next year. It flags a neutral-site game against Auburn on 5 September as potentially decisive.
Baylor Bears.outlook_dependency: Very high. Lagway is one of the two named reasons for optimism, and the guide ties the Over — and the head coach's job — to the season's outcome.

Cincinnati Bearcats.status: Transfer — from Georgia Southern, replacing Brendan Sorsby.
Cincinnati Bearcats.career_experience: Not addressed on Cincinnati's own pages. The Georgia Southern spread (p. 323) records him as that programme's all-time leading passer with 5,882 yards.
Cincinnati Bearcats.passing: Not addressed on Cincinnati's own pages. The Georgia Southern spread (p. 323) records a 20/8 touchdown-to-interception ratio with 2,929 yards.
Cincinnati Bearcats.rushing: Not addressed on Cincinnati's own pages. The Georgia Southern spread (p. 323) adds six rushing touchdowns.
Cincinnati Bearcats.efficiency: Characterized rather than quantified: an accurate passer who works underneath rather than a consistent deep-ball threat.
Cincinnati Bearcats.turnovers: Not addressed on Cincinnati's own pages; the Georgia Southern spread (p. 323) records eight interceptions.
Cincinnati Bearcats.competition: None described — French is presented as Sorsby's replacement.
Cincinnati Bearcats.author_confidence: Low, and stated as ignorance rather than judgement. The guide says it is hard to imagine what the offense looks like without Sorsby and sees a real chance of a massive step back.
Cincinnati Bearcats.positive_case: Characterized as an accurate passer who works underneath — the guide offers no stronger positive case than that.
Cincinnati Bearcats.concerns: He replaces a quarterback who threw for 2,800 yards with 27 touchdowns and five interceptions while adding 580 rushing yards and nine touchdowns, in an offense that ranked fifth nationally in Adjusted EPA per play at 0.14. French is not characterized as a consistent deep-ball threat, and the guide's conditional is that without an offense capable of generating explosive plays this becomes a long year.
Cincinnati Bearcats.supporting_cast: Weak. Top receiver Cyrus Allen, who had 13 touchdown catches, left for the Chiefs, and tight end Joe Royer also went to the NFL, leaving an underwhelming backfield and unproven receivers.
Cincinnati Bearcats.portal_context: French arrives from Georgia Southern; Sorsby, Allen and Royer all departed.
Cincinnati Bearcats.betting_implications: Recommendation is Under 5.5 wins. The guide credits the Nate Woody hire and instant-impact transfers with meaningfully changing the defense, while stating its conditional chain explicitly: without explosive plays this becomes a long year, and a long year for Cincinnati could mean a short one for Satterfield. It singles out a 5 September loss to Boston College as the result that could send the season off the rails.
Cincinnati Bearcats.outlook_dependency: Very high. The Under is argued primarily from the offense's uncertainty at quarterback after losing Sorsby.
Cincinnati Bearcats.conflicts: The guide notes candidly that it does not know what Sorsby will be doing in 2026 — his destination is left unstated.

Colorado Buffaloes.status: New starter — a five-star sophomore promoted from within.
Colorado Buffaloes.career_experience: Five-star and third-ranked quarterback in the 2025 class; appeared in parts of three games.
Colorado Buffaloes.previous_starts: Not addressed in guide as a start count; the guide records parts of three games.
Colorado Buffaloes.passing: 589 yards with four touchdowns and no interceptions across parts of three games.
Colorado Buffaloes.rushing: Not addressed in guide; the guide notes he is a traditional pro-style passer who will improvise less than Shedeur Sanders did.
Colorado Buffaloes.efficiency: Not addressed in guide; the guide characterizes the sample as neither great nor miserable.
Colorado Buffaloes.turnovers: No interceptions in the three-game sample.
Colorado Buffaloes.competition: None described as live, but the guide names a fallback: if Lewis' rise does not materialize, Utah transfer Isaac Wilson could get a chance.
Colorado Buffaloes.backup: Utah transfer Isaac Wilson, brother of Zach Wilson.
Colorado Buffaloes.author_confidence: Positive and forward-looking. The guide expects his rise to begin, while naming a fallback if it does not.
Colorado Buffaloes.positive_case: A five-star seen as the future of the programme, with the arm talent for the downfield throws Brennan Marion's system needs.
Colorado Buffaloes.concerns: A very small sample, and a style the guide expects to improvise less than his predecessor.
Colorado Buffaloes.scheme_fit: Described in detail. Marion's fast-paced power rushing 'Go-Go' system uses multiple backs and relies on fresh legs to break long runs inside, with rushing success setting up deep shots — and the guide says Lewis has the arm talent for those throws.
Colorado Buffaloes.supporting_cast: Good up front: two potential pros at tackle in Leon Bell and Bo Hughley plus proven starter Demetrius Hunter at center. The guide's judgement on the scheme is conditional on strong play from that group.
Colorado Buffaloes.portal_context: Colorado worked hard to bring reliable contributors through the portal, including Isaac Wilson from Utah at quarterback.
Colorado Buffaloes.betting_implications: Recommendation is Over 4.5 wins. The guide's reasoning is comparative — last year's roster lacked the talent to compete in the Big 12, while this group has the size, balance and skill to hang around — and it maps seven games from which Colorado needs four wins, rating that more likely than not.
Colorado Buffaloes.outlook_dependency: High. The guide frames the season as a test of whether the programme can succeed without Sanders' sons, which makes the new quarterback the central variable.

Houston Cougars.status: Returning starter — but the guide's framing question is how long he stays ahead of five-star Keisean Henderson.
Houston Cougars.career_experience: Established starter; the guide calls him solid.
Houston Cougars.previous_starts: Not addressed in guide as a start count.
Houston Cougars.passing: 2,705 yards with 25 touchdowns and nine interceptions.
Houston Cougars.efficiency: A 63.5 PFF throwing grade — the guide calls him a little inefficient as a passer.
Houston Cougars.competition: Not a declared competition, but the guide's headline question is whether Fritz can afford to keep Keisean Henderson on the bench all season.
Houston Cougars.backup: Keisean Henderson — a five-star who could have gone anywhere and chose Houston, an 18-year-old with top-tier mobility and a smooth delivery.
Houston Cougars.author_confidence: Qualified on the incumbent, openly tempted by the alternative. The guide credits Weigman as solid, then notes he was inefficient as a passer and struggled badly in some of Houston's biggest games.
Houston Cougars.positive_case: Solid dual production — 25 passing touchdowns plus 700 rushing yards and 11 scores — behind a much improved line.
Houston Cougars.concerns: Passing inefficiency at a 63.5 PFF grade and poor form in Houston's biggest games; the guide reasons that elite quarterback play could make Houston a legitimate national title contender, which makes playing Henderson tempting.
Houston Cougars.supporting_cast: Strong. Makhi Hughes heads a loaded backfield — 1,401 rushing yards and 15 touchdowns with 19 catches for 176 yards and two scores in 2024 at Tulane, among the best backs in the sport as a freshman and sophomore, before a non-factor season at Oregon where he redshirted after four games. Reunited with Fritz and running behind a much improved line, the guide expects him to return to stardom as the head of the snake. Houston has 19 projected starters who started in 2025.
Houston Cougars.portal_context: Makhi Hughes returns to Fritz from Oregon.
Houston Cougars.betting_implications: Recommendation is Over 7.5 wins — the guide notes the total is listed at either 7.5 or 8.5 depending on the book — and it goes further, calling this a team worth attacking with alternate lines and seeing a real chance of double-digit wins. Its market read is that road games at Texas Tech and Utah are the only two spots where Houston should be receiving points.
Houston Cougars.outlook_dependency: High on the upside. The guide states that elite quarterback play could make Houston a legitimate national title contender, making the position the difference between a good season and a great one.

Iowa State Cyclones.career_experience: A multi-year Arkansas State starter; the guide calls him a fun dual-threat there.
Iowa State Cyclones.previous_starts: Not addressed in guide on Iowa State's pages.
Iowa State Cyclones.passing: Not addressed on Iowa State's own pages. The Arkansas State spread (p. 333) records a career-best 3,361 passing yards on a Sun Belt-leading 501 attempts.
Iowa State Cyclones.rushing: Not addressed on Iowa State's own pages; the Arkansas State spread (p. 332) records 2.7 yards per carry.
Iowa State Cyclones.efficiency: Not addressed on Iowa State's own pages.
Iowa State Cyclones.turnovers: Characterized rather than counted: the guide says he turns the ball over too often.
Iowa State Cyclones.competition: None described — Raynor is presented as the starter.
Iowa State Cyclones.author_confidence: Low. The guide calls him exciting and a fun dual-threat while stating that little suggests he can carve up Big 12 defenses.
Iowa State Cyclones.positive_case: Exciting, and a fun dual-threat at Arkansas State.
Iowa State Cyclones.concerns: Turns the ball over too often, and the guide sees little evidence he can produce against Big 12 defenses.
Iowa State Cyclones.supporting_cast: Weak and unproven. Iowa State lacks proven pass catchers and has a shaky running back group behind a retooled line. That line added Braden Smith (Tarleton State), Caden Mass (Sioux Falls), Colin Amick (Montana) and Jake Taylor (Oklahoma) — but the guide notes the first three faced much weaker competition and Taylor missed all of last year after four starts, so there is no recent evidence.
Iowa State Cyclones.portal_context: Rogers hit the portal extremely hard for a mix of high-major players needing opportunity and successful lower-level players wanting a bigger stage; Raynor is the quarterback element of that.
Iowa State Cyclones.betting_implications: Recommendation is Under 4.5 wins. The guide expects wins over Southeast Missouri and Bowling Green, rates the road game at Iowa tough in year one, and finds it hard to identify three conference victories given how the offense looks on paper. It adds that with so many Big 12 teams looking to make leaps, Iowa State could be the punching bag.
Iowa State Cyclones.outlook_dependency: Very high. The Under is argued directly from how the offense looks on paper, with the quarterback the first element the guide doubts, and it states as a real possibility that this could be the worst offense in the Big 12.
